fish_response: Faster gill movement and reduced feeding response were first noted at 09:00 on 22 September, after nitrite-N had risen to 0.28 mg/L at the 06:00 check. Four dead fish were counted at 15:00, after the noon nitrite-N reading of 0.62 mg/L. Respiratory activity was less evident by the next morning, and no additional deaths were recorded from 18:00 on 22 September through 06:00 on 23 September.
evidence_gaps: Nitrite was measured only at discrete checks, so the exact onset and peak are unknown. Chloride concentration, confirmatory water tests, blood indicators, and gill examination results are missing. There is no pre- and post-backwash assessment of biofilter performance, no comparison raceway, and no record of the exact water-exchange completion time. The effects of water exchange and aeration cannot be separated, and other causes of mortality were not assessed in the record.
raw_question: Does the sequence support nitrite as a cause of the fish response and deaths, or could the rise be only associated with another event? What evidence would strengthen the diagnosis?
possible_causes: The rising nitrite-N is the leading water-quality candidate: it increased after the backwash and before the observed respiratory signs and deaths, while recorded DO, temperature, TAN, and flow remained stable. The timing is compatible with a nitrite-related effect, but does not prove that the backwash caused the rise or that nitrite alone caused the fish response. A post-backwash change in biofilter performance is a possible link, not a confirmed mechanism in this record.
raw_case_record: Raceway C-7 log, 21–23 September. At 06:00 on 21 September, DO was 8.3 mg/L, temperature 11.9°C, TAN 0.14 mg/L, nitrite-N 0.04 mg/L, and flow 100% of the usual rate. A biofilter backwash was completed at 09:00. At 18:00, DO was 8.2 mg/L, temperature 12.0°C, TAN 0.15 mg/L, nitrite-N 0.11 mg/L, and flow 100%. At 06:00 on 22 September, DO was 8.1 mg/L, temperature 12.0°C, TAN 0.15 mg/L, nitrite-N 0.28 mg/L, and flow 99%. Staff first noted faster gill movement and reduced feeding response at 09:00. At 12:00, nitrite-N was 0.62 mg/L; DO was 8.0 mg/L, temperature 12.1°C, TAN 0.16 mg/L, and flow 99%. Four dead fish were counted during the 15:00 check. Staff began a 20% water exchange at 13:00, added aeration as a precaution, and withheld the evening ration. At 06:00 on 23 September, nitrite-N was 0.31 mg/L, DO 8.2 mg/L, temperature 12.0°C, TAN 0.15 mg/L, and flow 100%. Respiratory activity was less evident, and no additional deaths were recorded between 18:00 on 22 September and 06:00 on 23 September. Chloride concentration, blood indicators, and gill examination results were not available.
causal_mechanism: Elevated nitrite can interfere with oxygen transport in fish, providing a plausible pathway from the rising nitrite-N readings to increased respiratory effort and, in severe cases, mortality. The sequence of rising readings followed by respiratory signs and deaths is consistent with that possibility. However, chloride concentration and fish blood or gill findings are absent, so the pathway is not demonstrated in these fish. The lower nitrite reading and reduced respiratory activity after water exchange are consistent with improvement, but the exchange and added aeration prevent attribution to one intervention.
timeline_summary: Before the 21 September biofilter backwash, recorded water-quality readings were stable. Nitrite-N rose from 0.04 mg/L at 06:00 on 21 September to 0.11 that evening, 0.28 at 06:00 on 22 September, and 0.62 at noon. Faster gill movement and reduced feeding response were noted at 09:00 on 22 September; four dead fish were counted at 15:00. DO, temperature, TAN, and flow remained nearly stable in the reported readings. A 20% water exchange began at 13:00, aeration was added, and the evening ration was withheld. By 06:00 on 23 September, nitrite-N was 0.31 mg/L, respiratory activity was less evident, and no additional deaths had been recorded during the stated interval.
diagnostic_answer: The timing makes the nitrite rise a plausible leading cause of the respiratory signs and deaths: nitrite-N increased before those observations, while recorded DO, temperature, TAN, and flow stayed nearly stable. The backwash may be related to the subsequent rise, but the record does not establish that it impaired biofilter function. Aeration is a coincident precaution rather than evidence of oxygen shortage, given the stable DO readings. The lower nitrite and fewer signs after water exchange are supportive but not conclusive because interventions overlapped. Chloride measurements, confirmatory nitrite testing, and fish-level diagnostic findings would strengthen or weaken the causal interpretation.
management_actions: A biofilter backwash was completed at 09:00 on 21 September. On 22 September, a 20% water exchange began at 13:00, aeration was added as a precaution, and the evening ration was withheld. The following morning, nitrite-N was lower and respiratory activity was less evident. The record does not give the exact completion time of the exchange.
water_quality_changes: Nitrite-N increased from 0.04 mg/L before the backwash to 0.11 mg/L by 18:00 on 21 September, 0.28 by 06:00 on 22 September, and 0.62 at noon. It was 0.31 mg/L at 06:00 on 23 September after a water exchange had begun. DO stayed between 8.0 and 8.3 mg/L, temperature between 11.9°C and 12.1°C, TAN between 0.14 and 0.16 mg/L, and flow at 99–100% of its usual rate. Readings were taken at discrete checks; chloride was not measured.
accompanying_phenomena: The biofilter backwash preceded the nitrite increase, but the record contains no direct measurement of biofilter function, so the backwash is a temporal association rather than a demonstrated cause. The four deaths occurred after the nitrite peak was recorded, but no fish-level diagnostic findings are provided. Aeration was added despite stable recorded DO and may have been precautionary; it is not evidence that low DO caused the event. Reduced feeding may be a response to stress, while withholding the evening ration was a management decision.
